replies.author: @globalonemusic2381
replies.text:
A STELLAR observation. :) BECAUSE of the isolation of many of these communities, the FIRST thing that crossed our minds were:
1) How far away is it to the nearest full service hospital ?
2) To the nearest Level One Trauma Center ?
3) To the nearest Pharmacy....let alone to a Pharmacy open late.....like in the U.S. ?
4) We were going to visit Zermatt in the summer, yet we were "nervous"  because although there ARE
Doctors there, most are Orthopedic, because it is a sky town in the winter. The reality is that the nearest
major hospital was almost 40 miles away. ANYONE over 50 should be somewhat nervous about that. :)
And then, we thought of the social isolation, even locally, that prohibits many people from creating
a valid "Neighbor Network", as such. The issue and the collateral issues you have brought up are those 
that the "Tourist Mindset" would never consider.
The Very Best to you. :)
Antoine

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: Thank you for sharing such a heartfelt and painful perspective. Beautiful mountains and peaceful villages can hide struggles that visitors may never see. No amount of wealth or natural beauty can replace human connection, especially for older people facing loneliness. Your words remind us that life in Switzerland has challenges beyond the picture-perfect scenery. We truly appreciate your honesty and hope you have people around you who bring warmth and companionship into your days. ❤️

And, one of the most interesting towns beside Zürich, which you also missed!, is Basel! 
Basel, - a truly international city/town, - is crossing borders with France & Germany!

replies.author: @HappyTravel99
replies.text: You're absolutely right! Lugano, Locarno, Ascona, and the beautiful lakes of Ticino certainly deserve more attention. And Basel, with its unique location at the meeting point of Switzerland, France, and Germany, is another fascinating place we wish we could have explored more. Switzerland has so much to offer that it's difficult to fit everything into one documentary. Thank you for pointing out these wonderful places and sharing your knowledge with us. We truly appreciate your feedback!
